technology.title: Nvidia Just Built a PC Chip That Runs AI Models Locally. Apple Should Be Nervous.
technology.excerpt: The RTX Spark, unveiled at Computex with MediaTek, packs a petaflop of AI power into a laptop. For Indian developers who've been buying MacBooks, the math just changed.
technology.image_caption: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose company just unveiled a desktop PC chip capable of running AI models locally (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: Indian developers and AI engineers in the US — the single largest national group in Silicon Valley's technical workforce — have overwhelmingly defaulted to MacBooks for local development. The RTX Spark's ability to run large language models locally on Windows, with 128GB unified memory and CUDA cores, could shift that calculus for the tens of thousands of NRI engineers building agentic AI systems.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's Startup Founders Are Stuck Between Seed and Scale. Global AI Is Hoarding the Capital.
technology.excerpt: A Series A squeeze is stranding India's best seed-funded companies as global venture capital floods into American AI labs. The numbers are stark.
technology.image_caption: Bengaluru, India's startup capital, where founders are struggling to raise Series A and B rounds as global AI startups absorb venture capital
technology.nri_angle: NRI investors and diaspora founders face a double bind: global VC capital that used to flow into India deals is being redirected to US AI companies, while Indian founders in the Bay Area trying to raise for India-focused startups find fewer co-investors willing to write Series A checks for non-AI businesses.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Wipro Sinks to a Three-Year Low as Oil at $97, AI Selloff, and Middle East Turmoil Converge
technology.excerpt: The IT bellwether fell 8.4 per cent in a single session, dragging the Nifty IT index down as three simultaneous shocks rattled Indian markets.
technology.image_caption: Wipro's Electronic City campus in Bangalore, India
technology.nri_angle: Indian IT workers face eroding ESOP values and retention bonuses. NRI investors suffer a double hit — falling stock prices in a weakening currency — though the rupee's slide makes Indian outsourcing cheaper for US clients.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: OpenAI Is Turning ChatGPT Into a Superapp. Its 900 Million Users Are About to Find Out What That Means.
technology.excerpt: Coding agents, task automation, and an enterprise pivot signal the biggest overhaul in ChatGPT's history — just as OpenAI prepares a confidential IPO filing.
technology.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman at a meeting in February 2025
technology.nri_angle: Indian developers are the world's fastest adopters of AI coding tools. The superapp's agentic capabilities could accelerate that trend — while threatening the offshore services model that employs hundreds of thousands.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Banks Are the Only Vertical Keeping Indian IT Alive. The FY26 Numbers Prove It.
technology.excerpt: BFSI now accounts for nearly a third of revenue at TCS, Infosys, and HCL — and it is the only segment growing while tech, telecom, and retail shrink.
technology.image_caption: Candlestick chart showing a downward trend in stock market analysis
technology.nri_angle: Over a million Indian IT workers — many on H-1B and L-1 visas in the US — are employed by these companies. Heavy BFSI concentration means a banking downturn would ripple through India's largest white-collar workforce.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Satya Nadella's Build Week Went Sideways. The Stakes Have Never Been Higher.
technology.excerpt: A leaked 'addiction' memo, a training-data scandal, and seven new in-house AI models — Microsoft's most important developer conference in a decade delivered fireworks nobody planned.
technology.image_caption: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella at a company event
technology.nri_angle: Satya Nadella remains the most powerful Indian-origin CEO in global tech. Microsoft employs tens of thousands of Indian engineers on H-1B visas across Redmond, Hyderabad, and Bangalore. Build 2026's push toward in-house AI models and agentic platforms directly shapes the roles — and job security — of this workforce.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Europe Just Built a Firewall Around Its Cloud. Indian IT's Biggest Clients Are on the Other Side.
technology.excerpt: The EU's new Technological Sovereignty Package creates a four-tier classification system for cloud services that could lock out American hyperscalers — and the Indian firms that depend on them.
technology.image_caption: The Berlaymont building in Brussels, headquarters of the European Commission which unveiled the cloud sovereignty proposals (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: Indian IT services giants — TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCL Tech — derive billions in revenue from European clients, largely through AWS, Azure, and GCP partnerships. A sovereignty framework that restricts hyperscaler access to sensitive EU contracts directly threatens this revenue stream and the thousands of Indian tech workers deployed in Europe.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Jensen Huang Called Marvell the Next Trillion-Dollar Company. Now It's Joining the S&P 500.
technology.excerpt: Marvell Technology enters the benchmark index after a 59% surge in two weeks, fuelled by an Nvidia endorsement, a custom AI chip boom, and a market that cannot get enough of the silicon behind the silicon.
technology.image_caption: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who called Marvell Technology a future trillion-dollar company (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: Indian chip designers are central to the custom silicon revolution powering Marvell, Broadcom, and hyperscaler in-house chip teams. Marvell's design centres in India contribute to the networking and optical interconnect chips driving its AI growth. For NRI investors, the S&P 500 inclusion triggers passive fund inflows that typically lift newly added stocks.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: T-Mobile Is Hiring 1,000 Engineers in Hyderabad. It Just Laid Off Hundreds in America.
technology.excerpt: The telecom giant opens a massive new tech hub in India the same quarter it cuts US workers — and it's far from alone. India's GCC boom is reshaping who builds American technology.
technology.image_caption: Glass architecture of a Hyderabad tech park, where T-Mobile's new GCC is located
technology.nri_angle: The GCC boom validates Indian engineering talent but accelerates offshoring that makes H-1B workers in the US anxious. Indian Americans sit uncomfortably at the intersection — their homeland's gain is sometimes their adopted country's loss.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk
